A_BOUND_WAS_FALSIFIED_AND_THE_CAUSE_WAS_: The duty-cycle factor's lower bracket assumes the floor run's minimum power lower-bounds every cell's sleep windows. VIOLATED ON 7 OF 19 CELLS - w64_d050_permissive, w64_d050_rep2, w64_d050_rep3, w64_d050_rep4, w96_d010, w96_d025, w96_d050 - whose sleep windows reach 3480-3600 mW against the floor run's 4113.4 mW minimum. Ten cells have a sleep SAMPLE below that minimum; only seven violate the energy bound. THE PREMISE IS FALSE BECAUSE THE COORDINATOR MEASURED THE FLOOR FIRST, AT THE CAMPAIGN'S HIGHEST FOREIGN LOAD, AND DID NOT RANDOMISE THE RUN ORDER. Recorded as FALSIFIED in VALIDATION.md, NOT as a pass, with the seven cells pinned as literals so any change to the set makes the script fail for real. THE GATE WAS NOT EDITED, NO THRESHOLD WAS MOVED AND NO CHECK WAS SKIPPED: the script exits 0 because it correctly establishes a falsification, which is a result, and exits non-zero if the falsification set ever differs from the pinned one. F depends on no floor figure at all - it is four measured integrals and two counts - and VALIDATION.md says so, which is what makes the falsification legible rather than alarming.
THE_RUN_ORDER_WAS_NOT_RANDOMISED_A_COORD: The 20 runs were sequential by frame dimension: floor, then five w48 duties, then five w64, then five w96, then three repeats, then the permissive control. Over the 29 minutes the board's 1-minute load average fell from 2.32 to 1.05, so FRAME DIMENSION IS CONFOUNDED WITH ELAPSED TIME AND WITH A FALLING FOREIGN LOAD, and the floor - measured first - was measured under conditions no later cell shared. w96_d010 draws 3716.75 mW WHILE RUNNING, BELOW the 4258.633 mW floor, and a check was written that FIRES on that condition so it cannot be overlooked. Nothing was re-run to hide it. A drift-adjusted variant substituting each cell's own sleep mean for the campaign floor makes the analytic model's ratios UNIFORM TO 0.0000 against absolute errors up to 0.1348 unadjusted - the ENTIRE scatter in that baseline is the floor drift - and it is published beside the measured figure, labelled an adjustment and used by nothing else. A FUTURE HARDWARE CAMPAIGN IN THIS MISSION MUST INTERLEAVE OR RANDOMISE ITS CELLS AND MEASURE THE FLOOR MORE THAN ONCE, AT THE START AND AT THE END AT MINIMUM.

CARRY_OVER_NEW_TONIGHT: (1) THE SENDMESSAGE RESUME PATH RETURNS NO USAGE BLOCK. Resuming an agent is the prompt's own prescribed recovery from a usage-limit termination, and it is also the right way to hand measured data to a running build - but the hand-back it returns carries no subagent_tokens, tool_uses or duration_ms, so the prompt's verbatim-accounting requirement cannot be met for any resumed round. Tonight the coordinator quoted 'nine cells' back to the agent as a finding; it was the agent's own pre-correction number and it was wrong. The rule that follows: a coordinator may only state a figure in a correction directive if it computed that figure itself in this session, and should say which. Measuring the floor once, first, under the highest foreign load of the session, falsified a bound and put the entire scatter of one baseline into one confound. Measure it at the start AND the end at minimum, and interleave the grid. (4) 60 SECONDS OF DRY RUN BOUGHT A CLEAN 27-MINUTE CAMPAIGN. Three of the last four hardware campaigns in this mission were discarded for instrumentation defects; this one was not, and the only difference was a dry run that asserted every output file existed with rows before the real campaign launched. Keep it.
